## Context / Problem
normalize_ci_conclusion.sh is a pure function in shell — trivially portable, currently tested only via a subprocess-driving contract test. Its REAL contract is two-input: f(CONCLUSION, FAILURE_OBSERVED) -> vote in {success, failure, cancelled} (never out-of-domain), consumed by .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml.

## Approach
Port to a small stdlib-only Python entry point with unit tests; the workflow call site swaps to the Python invocation. The existing contract test tests/scripts/test_normalize_ci_conclusion.py drives the SHELL script via subprocess — it is the porting oracle: first re-point its subprocess invocation at the Python entry point (proving CLI-level behavior parity env-var-for-env-var), keep its full case table, and add direct in-process unit tests of the function. The shell file is deleted in the same change, so no test ever references a missing script. The workflow currently fetches the script via sparse-checkout of exactly 'scripts/normalize_ci_conclusion.sh' (gerrit-verify.yaml:323) and calls it at :340 — update the sparse-checkout path to the new .py file (cone-mode: false so a single-file pattern works) and keep the entry point dependency-free so the single-file checkout still runs without the package installed. Opportunistic priority (lowest tier).

## Scope
- scripts/normalize_ci_conclusion.sh (deleted) -> new stdlib-only Python entry point
- tests/scripts/test_normalize_ci_conclusion.py: subprocess target swapped to the Python entry point, case table preserved
- .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml: sparse-checkout path at :323 AND the run invocation at :340
- new direct unit tests for the function

## Testing
The ported subprocess contract test keeps its full table (env-driven CLI parity). Direct table-driven unit test over f(CONCLUSION, FAILURE_OBSERVED):
- success -> success; failure -> failure; cancelled -> cancelled (FAILURE_OBSERVED irrelevant for these — assert both values)
- skipped x FAILURE_OBSERVED=false -> success (benign im-open fallback)
- skipped x FAILURE_OBSERVED=true -> failure (fail-closed)
- empty CONCLUSION -> failure; unrecognized value (e.g. 'timed_out') -> failure (fail-closed anomaly rows)
- FAILURE_OBSERVED unset defaults to false
Outputs asserted to always be in {success, failure, cancelled}.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Python entry point reproduces the shell mapping exactly as f(CONCLUSION, FAILURE_OBSERVED), including skipped-fallback rows and fail-closed empty/unknown rows.
- [ ] tests/scripts/test_normalize_ci_conclusion.py drives the Python entry point via subprocess with its case table preserved (no orphaned reference to the deleted .sh), plus direct unit tests cover the full contract (both FAILURE_OBSERVED values for pass-through rows included).
- [ ] gerrit-verify.yaml sparse-checkout fetches the new .py path (cone-mode: false) and the run step invokes it; entry point is stdlib-only so the single-file checkout works; shell file deleted.
